title: Life Without Sunlight
objective: After this level you can explain how life thrives around hydrothermal vents.
summary: At hydrothermal vents, microbes make food from hydrogen sulfide instead of sunlight. Giant tubeworms have no mouth: microbes inside them do the cooking.

cards.headline: In 1977, scientists found a crowd living where sunlight had never reached.
cards.body: Exploring the sea floor near the Galapagos Islands, they found hydrothermal vents, with animals living all around them. Every food web they knew began with sunlight. This one couldn't.

cards.headline: Food from chemicals
cards.body: Remember Level 8: below about 200 m there's too little light for photosynthesis. At a vent, microbes don't need it. They take hydrogen sulfide from the vent water and turn it into food. That's chemosynthesis, and tubeworms, shrimp and mussels all live on what the microbes make. Who needs the Sun when you have chemistry?

cards.headline: The worm with no mouth
cards.body: Giant tubeworms can stand nearly 2 m tall, yet they have no mouth and no gut. Instead, microbes live inside their bodies and turn vent chemicals into food, which they share with the worm. The tubeworm doesn't catch its dinner. It grows it in-house.

cards.headline: Same trick, different address
cards.body: Sound familiar? Level 56's whale bones work the same way: bacteria release hydrogen sulfide, and a whole community builds on bacteria instead of sunlight. Hot vents and old bones are very different places, but the recipe is the same. Wherever the deep offers chemical energy, life moves in.

cards.headline: Life without sunlight: explained
learned: Vents were found near the Galapagos in 1977

options.label: It filters shrimp out of the water
options.rationale: It has no gut to digest them.

Microbes inside it make food from vent chemicals
